name: Bluetooth
description: Windows MDM settings in the Bluetooth category, applied as OMA-URI (SyncML) values.

properties.name: Allow Advertising
properties.description: Specifies whether the device can send out Bluetooth advertisements. If this is not set or it is deleted, the default value of 1 (Allow) is used. Most restricted value is 0.

properties.name: Allow Discoverable Mode
properties.description: Specifies whether other Bluetooth-enabled devices can discover the device. If this is not set or it is deleted, the default value of 1 (Allow) is used. Most restricted value is 0.

properties.name: Allow Prepairing
properties.description: Specifies whether to allow specific bundled Bluetooth peripherals to automatically pair with the host device.

properties.name: Allow Prompted Proximal Connections
properties.description: This policy allows the IT admin to block users on these managed devices from using Swift Pair and other proximity based scenarios.

properties.name: Local Device Name
properties.description: Sets the local Bluetooth device name. If this is set, the value that it is set to will be used as the Bluetooth device name. To verify the policy is set, open the Bluetooth control panel on the device. Then, go to another Bluetooth-enabled device, open the Bluetooth control panel, and verify that the value that was specified. If this policy is not set or it is deleted, the default local radio name is used.

properties.name: Services Allowed List
properties.description: Set a list of allowable services and profiles. String hex formatted array of Bluetooth service UUIDs in canonical format, delimited by semicolons. For example, {782AFCFC-7CAA-436C-8BF0-78CD0FFBD4AF}. The default value is an empty string. For more information, see ServicesAllowedList usage guide

properties.name: Set Minimum Encryption Key Size
properties.description: There are multiple levels of encryption strength when pairing Bluetooth devices. This policy helps prevent weaker devices cryptographically being used in high security environments.
